name: Teresa Nielsen
life: “I sang my first solo behind a curtain because my shoes were borrowed.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the downtown fountain, where Teresa keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: My mother called it the kettle. I want to hear her recorded laugh alongside whatever name wins.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a mustard canvas overshirt and a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. Teresa has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Teresa listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
personality: Teresa thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Teresa sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To put the family's kettle name into the choir's programme.
family: Jasmine Boyd is Teresa’s second cousin. Teresa brings a spare shopping bag. Jasmine chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Care with a clock*, Jasmine says, “I borrowed a stopwatch to prove a point and found our client has a wonderful laugh at minute thirteen.”
connections: Jules Moran. The child's corrected note can sit beside the singer's memory of a mother's laugh.
